hints.title: Quadrant Decomposition and Homogeneity Validation
hints.text: A square grid is recursively partitioned into four equal sub-quadrants unless every cell within the active region shares the identical binary value.

hints.title: Divide and Conquer Grid Partitioning
hints.text: Check if the current subgrid is uniform. If all cells match, construct a leaf node with that value. Otherwise, divide into four subgrids of half width and recursively construct children.

hints.title: Recursive Subdivision Blueprint
hints.text: Function build(r, c, size): inspect grid cells from (r, c) to (r+size, c+size). If all equal val, return Node(val==1, True). Else half = size // 2, return Node(True, False, build(r, c, half), build(r, c+half, half), build(r+half, c, half), build(r+half, c+half, half)).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Recursive quad tree depth is log2(N) with cell equality scans across subregions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Flattening without geometric quadrant bounds makes quad-tree hierarchical subdivision ambiguous.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct recursive subgrid evaluation without auxiliary matrices limits memory to call stack depth.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct assignment of isLeaf and val properties on internal versus leaf nodes.
